topic: sub:11|Formulas and equations|Hours to reach zero BAC

6592.stem:
Josephine measures her mass to be 50kg.

On Saturday night she had 4 standard drinks in $2\dfrac{1}{2}$ hours.

The formula below can be used to estimate the BAC (Blood Alcohol Content) for females:

$$BAC_{\text{female}}=\dfrac{10N-7.5H}{5.5M}$$

where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking, and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

parts.latex: Show that Josephine's BAC was less than 0.08 after her last drink.

$$\text{Time}=\dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$$

The formula given above can be used to determine the number of hours required after a person stops consuming alcohol, for their BAC to reach zero. How many hours would Josephine require?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $N = 4$, $H = 2.5$, $M = 50$ into the formula.

$$\begin{aligned} BAC &= \dfrac{10 \times 4 - 7.5 \times 2.5}{5.5 \times 50} \\ &= 0.07727\ldots \end{aligned}$$

Since $0.07727\ldots < 0.08$, her BAC was less than $0.08$.

7154.stem: Sarah arrives at her friend’s birthday party at 6:00 pm and has her first standard drink. By 10:00 pm she has had another 4 standard drinks and decides to stop so that she can drive home at midnight.

parts.latex:
If Sarah weighs 75kg, calculate an approximate $BAC$ at 10 pm using the following formula, correct to two decimal places:

$$BAC_{Female} = \dfrac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$

Where,

$N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed

$H$ is the number of hours of drinking, and

$M$ is the person’s weight in kilograms.

The number of hours required for a person to reach zero $BAC$ after they stop consuming alcohol is given by the formula:

$$Time = \dfrac{BAC}{0.015}$$

Sarah is a P-plate driver and requires a $BAC$ of zero. Will she be able to leave at midnight and drive home? Justify your answer with mathematical calculations.

criteria: Substitutes correctly into the formula, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Use the time formula with the $BAC$ from part (i).
$$\begin{aligned} Time &= \dfrac{0.05}{0.015} \\ &= 3 \cdot \dot{3}\text{ hours} \\ &= 3\text{ h } 20\text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
(Using the unrounded value, $\dfrac{0.04848\ldots}{0.015} = 3.23\text{ h} = 3\text{ h } 14\text{ min}$.)

Sarah stopped drinking at 10 pm, so her $BAC$ reaches zero at about 1:20 am (1:14 am using the unrounded value).

No, she cannot leave at midnight; she should leave at 1:20 am.
